claims.text: The initial FeCoNi high-entropy alloy is single-phase fcc.
Introducing nanoprecipitates into single-phase fcc FeCoNi can increase its coercive field beyond 100 Oe.
Controlled heat treatment can introduce nanoprecipitates into single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
Mechanical alloying can introduce nanoprecipitates into single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
A heat treatment at 500–700 °C for 1–5 hours is an applicable processing window.
Mechanical alloying for 1–10 hours is an applicable processing window.
The intervention will produce nanoprecipitates 5–50 nm in size.
Domain-wall pinning by nanoprecipitates increases the coercive field.
The nanoprecipitate-containing alloy will have a coercive field at least 50% higher than single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi has a coercive field of 100 Oe or less.
The proposed compositional boundary permits additions of up to 5 at.% of elements other than Fe, Co, and Ni.
The proposed structural boundary is a nanoprecipitate size of 5–50 nm.
The predicted coercivity response is bounded to magnetic measurements at room temperature.
Nanoprecipitate composition and spatial distribution may affect coercivity.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis requires coercivity beyond 100 Oe, but the prediction and falsification rule require only a 50% relative increase from a baseline that may be substantially below 100 Oe. For example, an increase from 60 to 90 Oe would pass the stated relative criterion while failing the claimed beyond-100-Oe outcome.
